title: Your first report
text: Create a first draft from one source. Install the desktop app and open a separate workspace for sources, drafts, conversations and task records. In settings, select an installed, authenticated runtime and model. Confirm that your source may be sent to that service. Create a report. Specify the audience, date range, questions and target length, then add one public source. Start generation and follow progress in its task conversation. Open the saved draft, check citations, edit and save. Generate Word from the export menu. Download the completed file and open it in Word or WPS. Success means a saved draft version and a Word file you can open. A queued task or download button alone is not proof of completion. Without a model account, read these guides first. If your installed version offers a synthetic sample, it can demonstrate editing and export without a model; it is not an independently reviewed, model-generated report.

title: Install and update
text: Choose the right installer and preserve your workspace. Choose the Apple silicon DMG or Windows x64 EXE on the download page. Check About This Mac for the chip; browser Intel labels are unreliable. Prepare Python 3.11 or later. A compatible existing 3.12 installation is supported; the app neither requires a new 3.11 download nor installs system Python automatically. On Mac, copy the app to Applications. On Windows, run the installer. Follow the first-launch steps to prepare app-specific dependencies. Install and authenticate a model CLI separately. Desktop bridges use Electron’s built-in Node; WebUI bridge runtimes need Node.js 20+. Save drafts and back up the entire workspace while tasks are idle. Check updates in settings. On Mac, replace the app in Finder; Windows uses its installer. After restarting, check the app version and open the original workspace to confirm drafts and sources. The PyPI package provides the service and WebUI, not the desktop app. Initial Mac and Windows packages are unsigned; Mac packages are also not notarized. Verify the official source and SHA256, then use the OS permission for that app rather than disabling system protection. If updates fail, use official Releases; do not delete the workspace to fix a download.

title: Models and costs
text: Understand execution, data recipients and billing. A runtime is the local execution tool; a model is the generation service it connects to. Authenticate or configure its API first, then select it in BriefLoop. Use a model ID supported by that runtime. Saving settings is not a successful connection test; validate with a short public-text conversation. The main agent, Evaluator, Wiki Maintainer and Skill Proposer can use separate models. Evaluation and learning may also consume model usage. Set research limits, length and execution time. These are not a complete monetary cap; metering of runtime-native search varies. Check actual quotas and bills with the model and search providers. BriefLoop does not supply their subscriptions or model credits. The first conversation should return an actual response. New tasks use saved settings; queued and running tasks retain their original configuration. For quota errors, 429, 503 or an unknown model, inspect the task error and runtime authentication. Matching model names do not imply shared subscriptions. Read-only and network controls vary by runtime.

title: Write and edit reports
text: Move from sources and requirements to an editable draft. Create a report with its audience, purpose, period and required questions. Distinguish historical financial periods from current-month events. Add original sources; use search snippets only as discovery leads. Check dates, entities and definitions. Read conclusions and tables, then inspect key citations. Working drafts remain visible and downloadable even with low scores or unresolved review issues. Edit and save the body, or give BriefLoop specific revision instructions. Preserve the original and confirm that changes create a new version. Generate Word after saving. Export uses the saved version fixed when requested; later edits require another export. The body, version history and exported content should correspond. Edit in the browser and check final pagination in Word or WPS. If generation fails, inspect task logs and saved artifacts before recovering. Do not submit duplicate reports as a substitute for recovery. Unsaved edits do not appear in an earlier export.

title: Sources and review
text: Distinguish saved, linked, scored and reviewed content. Open citations to inspect the source title, date and excerpt, and consult originals where needed. For important figures, check entity, period, units, denominators and calculations. Preserve source conflicts rather than resolving them with a secondary summary. Read scores and specific findings for the current version; an old score does not automatically apply to a rewritten draft. If your version supports independent review, inspect its actual scope and unchecked items. A prompt alone cannot provide read-only isolation when the runtime lacks it. Ask BriefLoop to revise findings, or edit and save yourself, then check the new version. Downloading a working draft is separate from eligibility for formal delivery. Each resolved issue should correspond to a change in the new version, with review scope and unresolved issues visible. A source link or binding alone is not factual proof. Scanned PDFs, images and Excel formulas without cached values may need additional checks. Do not call a draft formally deliverable while it contains material errors, core evidence gaps or unresolved material conflicts.

title: Templates and charts
text: Manage writing methods, layout and chart data separately. Specify the report purpose and content before choosing a Word layout. A template name does not establish a specialized research workflow. Upload a DOCX for a company template and inspect recognized sections and manual fields. Supported layouts depend on the installed version. After table edits, check units, rows, columns and totals. Charts should retain sources and data periods. When asking BriefLoop to change complex charts, request checks against linked data; appearance alone does not verify values. Save, export and inspect fonts, pagination, table widths and captions in Word or WPS. The downloaded document should retain required sections and readable tables and figures. Layout changes and content edits are separate; verify the exported file. Complex Office objects, nested tables and multi-section templates may not be fully supported. Keep originals and inspect specific errors rather than assuming unsupported content was imported. The web editor is not a Word pagination preview.

title: Feedback and reuse
text: Turn specific revisions into inspectable, reversible experience. Explain the desired writing behavior or reason for a correction, including when it applies, rather than leaving only a score. Choose whether to enable automatic learning in settings and set the maximum rounds K. Additional rounds can increase model usage and time. Inspect Wiki experience and proposed skills. The Wiki holds method knowledge, not current-period evidence. Inspect validation results and adoption status. A candidate file does not mean it is active, and a running task does not demonstrate a benefit. If adoption is unsuitable, use the rollback control available in your version and confirm the active skill state. Preserve original feedback and comparison records. You should be able to distinguish feedback, candidates, validation and active content. Feedback can become experience evaluated for adoption; scores are not guaranteed to improve every round. When paused or out of quota, keep records and follow recovery instructions. Policies for explicit human requirements versus automated scoring suggestions vary by version; do not assume a development policy exists in an older installer.

title: FAQ and data
text: Preserve drafts, stop tasks and understand data transfers. Workspaces and records are stored locally. Cloud-model use sends relevant task, source, draft or feedback content to the selected service. Search queries go to the search provider and web requests to target sites. MCP parameters and necessary credentials go to the configured connector; local stdio programs may also access the network. Disabling public search does not stop model data transfers or guarantee network isolation for every runtime. Custom gateways and proxies may receive requests too. Use the app’s stop control and wait for a terminal state. Closing a browser does not stop an independent service; follow desktop save and task prompts when exiting. Back up the entire workspace while tasks are idle. Check materials and personal information before sharing logs, audit packages or folders, and exclude credentials. Saved drafts and sources should remain accessible after failure. Deleting local copies does not delete data already received by third parties; their retention rules depend on the service and account configuration. Diagnose HTTP 403, download and dependency errors by stage rather than repeatedly uninstalling and deleting workspaces. Record the version and error, use official releases and runtime diagnostics, and remove credentials and sensitive content before public support requests.
